clue.text: Smooth, low, captivating note

indicators.note: something captivating holds its object within, so the low word takes the note inside it

parts.note: feeling low is feeling sad

explanation.surface: A singer with a smooth, low, captivating voice holding a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand wood is to smooth it with abrasive paper, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Pro cultivating trees?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for

indicators.note: cultivating works the soil over, so the letters of trees are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what to call a professional who tends woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivating' rearranges the letters of trees; the whole clue also describes the answer, so it works as wordplay and definition at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland professional who plants and tends trees is exactly this job title.

clue.text: Server's trouble, unfortunately forgetting round

indicators.note: something going unfortunately goes wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
forgetting something leaves it out, so the round letter is dropped

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A waiter's bad luck, forgetting to bring a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' drops O from TROUBLE to leave TRUBLE, which 'unfortunately' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A household servant who serves wine and meals at table is a server in the domestic sense.

clue.text: Name put in coat from clever retailer

indicators.note: put in signals one piece is placed inside another
the coat of a word is its outside, so its first and last letters are taken

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: A name tag sewn into a coat bought from a smart shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat from clever' gives CR, the outer letters of clever, which hold HANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer who sells candles or ship's supplies is a type of shopkeeper.

clue.text: What soldier may have worn to pace around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: Asking what a soldier might wear when marching about.
explanation.definitionFit: A long military greatcoat or hooded cloak, once standard issue for soldiers, is this garment.

clue.text: Car benefiting driver leaving river behind

indicators.note: behind places the leftover letter after the first piece in this down entry

parts.note: something done for someone benefits them

indicators.note: leaving means the word river departs from driver, taking those letters out

explanation.surface: A car that suits a driver who has just left a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver leaving river' leaves D, put behind FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A make of motor vehicle from the American manufacturer founded by Henry of that surname.

clue.text: Sailing ship carrying nothing ornate

indicators.note: a ship carrying cargo holds it inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: a barque is a three-masted sailing vessel
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sailing ship with an empty hold but elaborate decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The highly decorated seventeenth-century style in art and architecture gives the word for elaborate.

clue.text: Criminal admits passion to deceive

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
heat is intense passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A crook confesses that desire drove them to trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to be unfaithful to a partner, a form of betrayal by deceit.

clue.text: Well-bred gentleman has an advantage

indicators.note: the phrase has the answer within its letters, spanning the join of two words

explanation.surface: A polite gentleman enjoys a head start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' shows the letters sit inside bRED GEntleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand over a rival is having this; the word also means a slight lead.

clue.text: Fill end on cracked carving resembling fabric

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Filling the end of a cracked carving made to look like cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor wood panelling carved to look like folded cloth is known by this name.

clue.text: Isn't solve exciting to get the down solutions!

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver complaining that cracking the puzzle is not thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exciting' rearranges ISNT SOLVE. Every down answer in the grid is a writer of fiction: Sand, Forester, Butler, Twain and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The theme: each down entry in this puzzle is the surname of a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Did model dishearten younger, lusty fellow?

parts.note: an artist's model sat for a portrait

indicators.note: to dishearten a word is to remove its heart, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Did posing for an artist depress a lecherous younger man?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishearten' strips out the inside of younger, keeping only its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these goat-like woodland creatures were notorious for lechery, hence any lecherous man.

clue.text: Genius dismissing what he'd call a mug

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the archetypal genius
Einstein was German, and the German word for a is ein

explanation.surface: A clever person rejecting what they'd call a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug looks like a dupe; it is a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large earthenware beer tankard, often lidded, as served at German beer festivals.

clue.text: Balt featured in nasty Victorian story

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: vile means nasty
a Lett is a Latvian, one of the Baltic peoples

explanation.surface: A Baltic character appears in an unpleasant nineteenth-century tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's 1853 novel set in a Belgian school is this book.

clue.text: Old couple needing time on the wagon

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a wain is an old farm wagon

explanation.surface: An elderly pair needing a spell off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' looks like teetotal; the wagon is a farm cart.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for two or a pair, as in never the twain shall meet.

clue.text: Try hard with something corny?

parts.note: H is short for hard, as on pencils
an ear of corn is the seed-bearing head

explanation.surface: Making an effort with a hackneyed joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge tries a case by listening to it in court, the legal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Office worker, one doing her nails?

definitions.meaning: a clerk who files documents away
a nail file, the tool used to shape fingernails

explanation.definitionFit: A clerk who sorts papers into cabinets, and also the emery board used in a manicure.

clue.text: Playing cricket, competitors now favoured golf

parts.note: the field is everyone competing in a race
in means fashionable, currently popular
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports report: the cricket match underway while the players prefer golf.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the side not batting is stopping and returning the ball, the activity of the fielders.

clue.text: Alcohol and nuts spiked with drug

indicators.note: a drink spiked with something has it slipped inside

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drink and snacks laced with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient fermented drink made from honey and water is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: One girl or another at the French seaside?

indicators.note: another girl at the seaside is placed after the sea word, so at sets the order

parts.note: mer is French for sea
another girl, Edith

explanation.surface: Wondering which of two girls is on holiday at a French beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'another at the French seaside' as Edith placed after MER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh name used for girls, as with the actress Meredith Baxter.

clue.text: We pass on perverted, seedy things

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We ignore sleazy, depraved people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' rearranges WE PASS ON. 'Seedy' seems to mean sleazy; here it means full of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout pods, eaten whole with their small seeds, are literally things full of seeds.

clue.text: He exercises command over two monarchs

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upside down, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a law is a command or decree
K for king and ER for Elizabeth Regina, two monarchs

explanation.surface: A man whose workout lets him rule over two kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes for walks takes exercise on foot, so the doer of that exercise.

clue.text: Advanced spin-doctoring working as protection

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of spin
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Media spin used as a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment tied over the front of clothes shields them from spills in the kitchen.

clue.text: Group of stars, one parading topless

indicators.note: topless removes the top letter, the first in a down entry

parts.note: a marcher parades in a procession

explanation.surface: A troupe of celebrities, one of them marching without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittarius, the constellation pictured as a bowman, is known by this name.

clue.text: Dead ends from copper, drug affair regressing

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
LSD is the hallucinogenic drug

indicators.note: regressing means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a case is an affair or matter

explanation.surface: A police officer's drug case going backwards and getting nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets closed at one end lead nowhere, so they are literally ends with no way through.

clue.text: Grant for films runs out of support

indicators.note: out of means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: to carry is to support a weight
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Film funding exhausts its backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant for films' looks like money; it is the Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the Hollywood leading man known on screen as Grant.

clue.text: Peer expected to pocket a thousand

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: due means expected, as in due to arrive
K is short for a thousand

explanation.surface: A nobleman anticipated to scoop a grand.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest rank of the British peerage, a nobleman ranking above a marquess.

clue.text: Requesting to put away a second piece

indicators.note: to put away is to remove, so these letters are taken off

parts.note: requesting is asking
A taken as written and S, short for second

explanation.surface: Asking someone to tidy away another item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put away' removes A and S from ASKING.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important man on a chessboard is a chess piece.

clue.text: Soldiers list second site of English defeat

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: Troops are tilting a second time where the English were beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city whose 1429 siege Joan of Arc lifted, a famous defeat for the English army.

clue.text: Don't admit catching the clap? It's what you get in life

definitions.text: It's what you get in life

indicators.note: catching means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to deny is to refuse to admit
the clap is slang for gonorrhoea, an STI or sexually transmitted infection

explanation.surface: Denying you caught gonorrhoea, as if it were simply fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate, the course of events that awaits each person, is what life deals you.
